subject.title: fix(hooks): prevent Codex relay resource exhaustion

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this new default minimal-process relay architecture for Codex hooks after the failing topology/dependency gates are resolved and the Codex lifecycle contract is reviewed?
rationale: This is a broad runtime-boundary change rather than a localized bug fix: it changes how existing hook commands start, read registration data, and fail during gateway/relay lifecycle races.

options.title: Sponsor the fast relay path
options.body: Require the failing gates, direct Codex contract comparison, and install/upgrade runtime proof, then continue with this architecture.

options.title: Keep the full CLI path
options.body: Retain the current command path and pursue a narrower resource-bound fix inside the existing relay process.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the fast relay path
recommendation.body: Require the failing gates, direct Codex contract comparison, and install/upgrade runtime proof, then continue with this architecture.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent Codex relay work makes this the best available owner signal for the runtime-boundary decision.
